body:
Cashier operations need durable replay receipts, an exact actor/venue/shift boundary and consistent booking prices. Owner onboarding needs stable resource identities and venue-specific review revisions; existing client table grants also require containment.

This draft contains backend integrity repairs against backend/playspot-core-v2: wallet/payment and session-close safeguards, profile write restrictions, versioned venue review and resumable drafts, active super-admin checks, cashier ownership/online availability, partial cash collection, ordered device-bound fixed reserve/start/item-order/cash/close reconciliation, and financial/table-management privilege hardening.

Fixed-session reconciliation separates actual room occupancy from agreed billing through server-owned close/timezone fields and a generated capacity range. Early close releases remaining capacity without changing price or marking debt paid. The coordinator checks saved room/time/balance snapshots, exact permissions/shift, canonical quotes, existing tournaments and replay ordering. Account-free walk-ins require booking authority; registered first customers retain prepaid policy. Canonical active super-admin permissions now match writer issuance and private booking authorization. Issuance holds shared profile/Auth locks; native races prove revocation waits, then immediately closes public availability. Disabled/banned/deleted identities and removed admin memberships remain denied. Hosted price-trigger repricing rolls back reservations, transitions, orders and cash rather than silently changing balances.

Writer refresh, booking admission and reconciliation now share a venue transaction lock before writer row locks, including first claims without an authority row. The booking guard also locks the writer row and evaluates lease expiry against the current wall clock after waiting. These paths explicitly require READ COMMITTED; unverified REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE snapshots fail closed. Legacy existing-booking RPC and multi-venue lock ordering still need full-schema review.

Validation: the six affected native PostgreSQL 17.11 suites pass 235 cases: 51 writer/availability, 25 cash reconciliation, 34 item-order reconciliation, 53 fixed-session reconciliation, 25 immutable-permit lifecycle and 47 partial-cash collection. Real independent connections and a separate fixture-admin observer prove lock waiting, both booking/offline-transition orderings, first writer claims, heartbeat expiry during a wait, and both offline-reservation/refresh orderings. The prior availability source was reproduced admitting a competing booking before an offline refresh committed. Financial privilege/RLS and table-management suites previously passed 34 and 43 cases. Exported native wire responses pass the dashboard foundation tests (491 offline tests, two live tests skipped). Fixtures have synthetic Auth/permissions and incomplete hosted audit/moderation/notification/loyalty/RLS behavior; this is not hosted end-to-end proof.

Release blockers: no hosted SQL has been applied. The new capacity column/exclusion index requires data/lock/deployment planning and discovery adapters. Immutable 24-hour permit generations now preserve original issue windows and permissions. Renewal cannot extend or rewrite an old grant; reconciliation accepts eligible historical operations and rejects backdating. The dashboard has scoped encrypted history, ordered authority refresh and authenticated/logout guards. Canonical snapshots/device bootstrap, shift lifecycle/reconciliation, conflict review and real offline cashier read/action wiring remain incomplete. DST crossing/ambiguous intervals require review. Open-time/extensions, mixed payments/refunds, combos and advanced pricing require coordinated contracts. Supabase-admin-owned default ACLs need separate owner handling. Owner creation, legacy KYC/canteen endpoints and the broader Phase 6/7 baseline still need review. Dashboard PRs #53/#54 require coordinated rollout.

Keep this PR draft. No dev/main merge, force push or automatic migration is included.

### Integrated into dev for testing (2026-10-02)

The complete head commit is an ancestor of dev at `93ae37f48e4563d06e2e0f67d002181aab745ac9`. Closed after the user-authorized dev integration to avoid leaving a duplicate request targeting main or the old backend base. No main merge or hosted SQL deployment was performed. Newly introduced backend SQL remains under `supabase/review/migrations/`; see `docs/DEV_TESTING.md` for local verification and production blockers.

A failed attendance action restored an entire old request list, losing newer Realtime arrivals or undoing another successful action. Repeated taps could send duplicate mutations. After reviewing an extension, the data source permanently hid its booking-based ID, also hiding subsequent requests for that booking.

Roll back only the optimistic item that has not been replaced by a fresh server snapshot, guard pending attendance per request/scope, and let server extension status govern future visibility.

Validation: four new regressions reproduced the defects before fixes. Full Flutter suite: 1256 passed / 2 skipped. Full formatting passed; analysis passed with no issues before the final small data-source/test change (CI rechecks final head). No schema, pricing, or persisted financial changes.

body:
## Confirmed issue
`SessionOperationsRemoteHelper.reviewExtensionRequest` returned `void` without a backend call when a request carried a malformed booking UUID. The caller interpreted that as success and could mark the request attended. It also ignored JSON `success:false`/invalid acknowledgement. `ClientRequestParser.parseBookingExtension` mapped the RPC's display `id=ext_<uuid>` to bookingId instead of using its canonical `booking_id`.

## Changes
- Prefer canonical `booking_id`, normalizing `ext_` legacy identifiers safely.
- Require a fully matching UUID for staff review (canonical UUID or `ext_` prefix only). **Throw**, never silently return, on malformed IDs.
- Only consider `approve_booking_extension` / `reject_booking_extension` successful after server acknowledgement `success==true`.
- Add remote HTTP MockClient tests for valid approve/reject, invalid UUID no-op, and malformed/failed backend acknowledgement. Add parser tests for canonical and legacy IDs.

## Safety
No modifications to prices, extension durations, Supabase production schema, financial rows or staff permission policies. Wait for dashboard CI quality gates before merging.

body:
Cashier screens currently depend on online repositories. This draft adds actor/venue-scoped local storage and ordered reconciliation for walk-in bookings, sessions, product orders and cash, together with a responsive session workspace.

Encrypted Hive retains projection/inventory/receipts/outbox atomically. Journal keys use FlutterSecureStorage; GetStorage holds non-secret settings. Commands bind original quotes, operation IDs, shift, actor, device and immutable permit generation. Partial cash, room eligibility/overlap, overdue occupancy and early close preserve agreed prices and debt. Sequential single-flight synchronization verifies canonical receipts before atomic projection writes and preserves conflicts and later optimistic operations.

Protocol 2 authority refresh validates scope, original 24-hour grant windows, server/device clocks, permissions, heartbeat mode and monotonic sequence. Permit history cannot be rewritten; pending historical operations survive renewal/reopen. Auth changes invalidate outstanding requests and store references; logout closes journals without deleting their files. Invalid historical records remain on disk and block new commands for review.

The cashier workspace separates session rail, responsive facts, header/actions, payments and requests. Desktop/tablet use a split view; mobile uses an owned details sheet that closes on workspace removal. Manage remains reachable at large Arabic text sizes. Request/next-booking details remain tenant scoped. Open-time elapsed duration no longer creates deadline urgency. A deterministic shared clock reaches modal details; classification avoids unchanged parent rebuilds.

Validation: 491 offline Flutter tests passed, including 248 offline-cashier cases and 23 secure-auth cases with encrypted temporary Hive files and native exported contract fixtures. The same two live database tests are skipped. Analyze has 21 existing informational findings and no errors/warnings. Formatter/diff checks passed; generated plugin/cache artifacts were excluded. Layout/group/grid coverage has 46 cases and 28 synthetic Flutter PNGs at 360/600/768/1024/1440 with Arabic/English, Tajawal and text scale 1.0/1.6. A Windows debug widget fixture with 100 sessions across 45 simulated seconds measured zero workspace/details builds and 360 clock-leaf builds; it is not device frame/FPS evidence. Backend PR #41 has 176 current writer/permit/cash/item/fixed native cases; fixed-session suite has 53 cases. Historical permit fixture data is reconstructed from canonical immutable rows, not a hosted capture.

Supabase sessions and new PKCE verifiers now use explicit endpoint-scoped FlutterSecureStorage adapters, with verified legacy migration, selective logout and no destructive Android reset. Same-account SIGNED_IN invalidates old requests and journals; opening drains the latest closing chain, while token refresh preserves identity. Twenty-three storage cases and two separate native Android API 36 probe processes passed using synthetic data; production mobile manifest merge also passes. Actual account, physical device, web/iOS/Windows verification and existing plaintext profile caches remain follow-up work. Companion mobile PR is playspot_V2#42.

Logout reference-cache cleanup owns only cache_* keys and drains earlier writes before removal. Settings and unrelated legacy auth keys survive; cleanup failures return a localized CacheFailure rather than escaping the repository. Eleven additional offline cases cover delayed writes, corrupt entries, invalid keys and all remote/local logout outcomes. docs/LOCAL_CACHE_AUDIT.md records remaining plaintext profile/onboarding caches and the dashboard LoginCubit's discarded logout result.

Release blockers: real cashier actions/read repositories still use online paths. Canonical room/inventory/booking/shift bootstrap, cached adapters, heartbeat availability UI integration, conflict review, shift close/reassignment, open-time/extensions, mixed payments/refunds and advanced pricing remain incomplete. Confirmed collected/due values are intentionally unavailable until the canonical finance adapter exists. Secure-auth source and Android plugin probes pass; actual account and remaining platform credential storage need verification. Backend salahaldensherief/playspot_V2#41 is source-only; no SQL has been deployed. Capacity range/exclusion changes require data/lock/deployment planning and discovery adapters. Existing experimental incomplete records remain retained for review.

Keep this PR draft until actual UI/backend/device workflows pass. No SQL deployment or dev/main merge is included.
